publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/cronSkipWatchdogPrefix.test.ts (5). The cron file touched is cronSkipWatchdog.ts, and the change does NOT move a decision point: it widens a DETECTOR so an existing alarm can see a second string. No job gains or loses the ability to run, no gate direction changes, and no customer-facing path is altered — the watchdog only reads cron_log and reports. Fail-closed direction is therefore unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION, and the tests pin the property that actually matters: the matcher must recognise BOTH strings the scheduler can write. It matched only the literal requiresEnv:, while unarmedFlagReason emits requiresFlag:KEY (why) — and requiresFlag is what guards the whole reel/social publishing pipeline (REEL_GENERATION_ENABLED, REEL_AUTOPOST_ENABLED, SOCIAL_INVENTORY_PUBLISH_ENABLED, CONTENT_REPLENISH_ENABLED), so those four were invisible to the one watchdog built for them. Not hypothetical: a Railway variable for that pipeline was deleted on 2026-08-03 and a variable delete does not restart the container; had it been REEL_GENERATION_ENABLED, reels would have gone dark with NO alarm anywhere, because the failure observer counts only status=failed and an unarmed job logs skipped. The tests build their expected strings from the REAL emitter (unarmedFlagReason imported from the scheduler) rather than hand-copied literals, because copying a literal is precisely the mistake the watchdog made; they cover an absent flag, a flag set to the WRONG value (1 instead of true — the live two-convention trap in this repo), the correctly-armed case returning null so no false alarm fires, and a source-text pin on the matcher itself since the regex-shape tests would still pass if someone narrowed the file back. KNOWN AND NOT CHANGED, stated so it is not mistaken for coverage: cronSkipWatchdog.ts line 100 skips any job with even one completed run in the 7-day window, so a job that alternates armed and unarmed still evades it; widening that risks alarm noise and was left for a deliberate decision. ALSO REFUTED THIS SESSION, recorded because it nearly became a change: an earlier analysis claimed the retention crons were silently idle on the basis of records_processed = 0. Reading cron_log.details refutes it — followup-cadence logs No completed bookings in window (15 runs) and Outside call window Cleveland 7:00 window 9-18 (12 runs), and alg-declined-work-recovery is actively sending with a holdout control arm against a $45,800 pool. FEATURE_FOLLOWUP_CADENCE is already correctly set to 1 in prod, as are its three siblings; no flag was flipped. Verified: 5 tests green, pnpm run check exit 0, pnpm run verify exit 0.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — the command palette (Cmd+K on desktop, the floating Zap button on the phone). BEFORE: the palette offered every admin section and all 23 navigating quick actions to every role. Admin.tsx has always gated onNavigate with allowedSections, so for a front_desk / tech / accountant / viewer login the forbidden entries rendered, took the tap, closed the palette, and did nothing — a silent no-op door (front_desk: 10 of 16 sections were dead; viewer: 13 of 16). Recorded as open in the cadence-and-admin memory ('CommandSearch derives shortcuts from the registry but ignores role'). AFTER: the palette derives its offering from the SAME sectionsForRole(adminRole) array Admin.tsx gates with — section shortcuts filter by allowedSections, and every navigating quick action now declares its target section and hides when the role cannot reach it. Drilldowns and direct mutations (no navigation) stay visible to all roles; server-side permission checks remain the authority for those. For the owner/manager (the operator's own login) the palette is UNCHANGED — all 16 sections, all actions — pinned by the 'owner still browses the full registry' test. WALKTHROUGH STATUS: DEFERRED-LIVE with reason — this session is a remote agent run with no phone in hand and no restricted-role credential to log in with; the behaviour is pinned instead by client/src/__tests__/commandPaletteRoleTruth.test.ts (15 tests, derived from sectionsForRole rather than hand-kept lists), MUTATION-VERIFIED: unfiltering visibleSectionShortcuts turns 5 tests red, reverting returns 15/15 green. adminRegistryTruth.test.ts (20) still green alongside. tsc --noEmit exit 0. NOT CLAIMED: no live restricted-role login was performed; the owner-facing surface is asserted unchanged by test, not by phone.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited — and the reason is the point of the diff. The rule fires on 15 files under server/services/**, but 13 of those are DELETIONS of modules that production never reached, and the other two are comment-only edits explaining where a deleted module went. A capability the ledger tracks is one the shop can USE; these were unreachable from any entry point, so removing them cannot change a capability state. Verification, four ways, re-run AFTER merging 13 commits of sibling work in case one had been wired meanwhile: zero import statements anywhere in server/, client/src/, shared/ or scripts/; zero test importers; zero references in package.json, vitest.config.ts or tsconfig.json; and no template-literal dynamic imports exist anywhere in server/ for a path-built import to hide behind. Deleted: absurdityEngine, aiContentGenerator, citationManager, competitorPricing, customerLookup, integrationDashboard, leadScoring, nexusAuditor, noShowPrediction, notificationRouter, serviceMemory, smartScheduler, vapi-personalization — 2,228 lines. FOUR NEAR-MISSES recorded because the first scan would have caused damage: (1) a SYMBOL-level scan reported 245 unwired exports and two of the three I spot-checked were false — computeRetentionCohorts and loopShapeContract are both imported in production via a different export than the one flagged — so the scan was redone at MODULE level, giving 24 candidates rather than 245; (2) blog-seeder/runner.ts looked dead and is NOT, because package.json:27 runs it as test:ai-evals and lint-source.mjs:45 allowlists it — a script path, invisible to any import-based scan — so it was excluded; (3) invoiceGenerator, financingPreQual and quoteEngine sit in the vitest.config.ts coverage include list, the money-path set measured against thresholds, so three revenue-named modules were deliberately placed in a money gate despite having no importers — that is operator intent I cannot read from code, and all three are LEFT IN PLACE; (4) three deleted modules were cited BY NAME in comments elsewhere, so winbackProcessor.ts, winbackOptOut.test.ts, vapi-bdi.ts and shared/customerDimension.ts now record that the module was removed and where its rationale survives, rather than leaving a citation pointing at a file that no longer exists. NOT CLAIMED: this does not assert the deleted ideas were bad, only that production could not reach them. Verified: pnpm run check exit 0 (the config that includes tests, which verify does not), full pnpm run verify exit 0, and no dangling reference to any deleted module remains outside the four explanatory notes.

render-spend-trajectory.ref: NO SPEND CHANGES IN THIS DIFF, and that is the claim being made rather than dodged. The rule fires because services/higgsfieldStudio.ts is touched, so here is exactly what was touched in it.  materializeStartImage's inline SSRF guard and bounded-read loop were EXTRACTED to lib/publicFetch.ts and are now called instead of inlined — 126 lines removed, zero rules changed. The extraction is byte-faithful: the same CIDR-parsed IPv4 blocks, the same IPv4-inside-IPv6 handling, the same FQDN-root-dot strip, the same per-hop revalidation, the same START_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES cap and START_IMAGE_MAX_REDIRECTS limit passed in as options. The now-unused `isIP` import was dropped.  Nothing on the generation or billing path is touched. No reservation is created, settled or released differently; reelClipCostUsd, COST_ESTIMATES_USD, reelLedgerModel and every reserve/settle call site are untouched by this diff. materializeStartImage is a DOWNLOAD of an already-generated frame — it makes no provider call and books no cost — and its failure contract is unchanged: every failure still returns null and the clip renders text-only, because conditioning is an enhancement that must degrade a reel rather than break it.  The only behavioural difference is which module the same refusals come from, which is why the check that matters is the existing suite rather than a new spend assertion: higgsfieldStudio's 53 tests pass unchanged, and the extracted rules gained 17 of their own in server/publicFetch.test.ts (they previously had none of their own — they were reachable only through materializeStartImage).  Full serial suite: 394 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,879 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean. NOT CLAIMED: no live spend trajectory, no provider call, no production render — nothing here was measured against generation_reservations.
